1	\section{Conclusion}
2	
3	We present the first systematic per-example analysis of how attention affects cross-architecture agreement in hybrid recurrent models. Aggregate convergence is task-specific (only LAMBADA among ten benchmarks) and scale-dependent (monotonic at 1.3B, non-monotonic at 340M). Per-example predictive multiplicity, however, is observed on both a retrieval task (LAMBADA) and a mixed task (ARC-Easy) in three architectures ($\alpha \approx 0.21$--$0.30$), independent of aggregate convergence. The low per-example overlap (Jaccard $\leq 0.14$) suggests that, if confirmed in additional architectures and benchmarks, diverse hybrid ensembles may provide complementary coverage. Future work should establish causal mechanisms through attention ablation and extend the analysis beyond these three architectures.

7	We use the pretrained model zoo of \citet{wang2025hybrid}, which provides controlled comparisons across architectures and attention ratios. The zoo contains three linear recurrent architectures: GatedDeltaNet \citep{yang2024gateddeltanet}, RetNet \citep{sun2023retnet}, and HGRN2 \citep{qin2024hgrn2}. These three architectures represent distinct approaches to linear recurrence: GatedDeltaNet uses gated delta rules, RetNet uses multi-scale exponential decay, and HGRN2 uses gated linear recurrence with state expansion. Each architecture is trained at five attention ratios: 0\% (pure recurrent), 4\%, 7.7\%, 14.3\%, and 25\%. We adopt the h$k$-1 notation from the original work, where one attention layer is interleaved per every $k{+}1$ total layers: h3-1 corresponds to 25\% attention, h6-1 to 14.3\%, h12-1 to 7.7\%, and h24-1 to 4\%. All configurations are available at two scales: 340M and 1.3B parameters. Within each scale, all models share identical training data, tokenizer, and hyperparameters; they differ only in architecture and attention configuration. This controlled design isolates the effect of attention from confounds such as training data or optimization differences. The zoo also includes a Transformer baseline (pure attention) at both scales.

We conduct a systematic analysis using the controlled model zoo of \citet{wang2025hybrid}: three architectures (GatedDeltaNet, RetNet, HGRN2) at five attention ratios and two scales (340M and 1.3B parameters), evaluated on 10 benchmarks with per-example analysis on LAMBADA ($N = 5{,}153$) and ARC-Easy ($N = 2{,}376$). Aggregate convergence is task-specific: only LAMBADA shows monotonic reduction in cross-architecture variance ($\rho = -1.0$, BCa 95\% CI $[-1.0, -0.7]$; $\sigma$ drops 79\%; Bonferroni-adjusted $p = .100$), complete at 1.3B but non-monotonic at 340M. Per-example predictive multiplicity, however, is general: on both benchmarks, architectures help and hurt different examples when attention is added (Jaccard $\leq 0.13$, all $p < .01$; ambiguity $\alpha \approx 0.21$--$0.30$ stable across attention ratios). On LAMBADA, aggregate and per-example trajectories are decoupled: $\sigma$ decreases gradually while per-example overlap saturates at 4\% attention. On ARC-Easy, per-example divergence persists without any aggregate convergence ($\rho = -0.20$, n.s.). These results establish predictive multiplicity \citep{marx2020predictive} across two task categories (retrieval and mixed) in three linear recurrent backbones, independent of aggregate performance equalization.

Aggregate convergence is task-specific: only LAMBADA shows monotonic reduction in cross-architecture variance ($\rho = -1.0$, BCa 95\% CI $[-1.0, -0.7]$; $\sigma$ drops 79\%; Bonferroni-adjusted $p = .100$), complete at 1.3B but non-monotonic at 340M. Per-example predictive multiplicity varies in magnitude but is present on all four benchmarks: the ambiguity $\alpha$ \citep{marx2020predictive} ranges from 0.10 (HellaSwag) to 0.49 (BoolQ), forming a task-dependent spectrum rather than a binary phenomenon, while pairwise Jaccard of helped/hurt sets remains universally low ($\leq 0.13$, all $p < .01$). On LAMBADA, aggregate and per-example trajectories are decoupled: $\sigma$ decreases gradually while per-example overlap saturates at 4\% attention. These results establish per-example predictive multiplicity across all four task categories (retrieval, comprehension, reasoning, mixed) in three linear recurrent backbones, with HellaSwag's near-zero $\alpha$ serving as a reference point that rules out measurement noise.

82	
83	The central finding of this paper is that aggregate convergence and per-example divergence operate on different timescales as attention ratio increases (Figure~\ref{fig:decoupling}).
84

82	
83	The central finding of this paper is that aggregate convergence and per-example divergence operate on different timescales as attention ratio increases (Figure~\ref{fig:decoupling}).

85	Cross-architecture $\sigma$ decreases gradually across the five attention ratios: $0.024 \to 0.016 \to 0.014 \to 0.006 \to 0.005$. In contrast, pairwise Jaccard similarity between architectures' per-example effects saturates at the first attention level (4\%): approximately 0.095 for helped, with no further increase at higher ratios. Net asymmetry between architectures' per-example profiles increases from 0.013 at 4\% attention to 0.040 at 25\%.
